questions.text:
Consider the Karnaugh map given below, where x represents "don't care" and blank represents 0.

Assume for all inputs (a, b, c, d) the respective complements [latex](\bar{a},\bar{b},\bar{c},\bar{d})[/latex] are also available. The above logic is implemented 2-input NOR gates only. The minimum number of gates required is ____________.
questions.solution:
The 1s (with suitable don't-cares) form one group: all cells with c = 1 and a = 0. So [latex]f=c\bar a[/latex].

[latex]c\bar a=\overline{\bar c+a}=NOR(\bar c,a)[/latex] [latex]\text{---}[/latex] a single 2-input NOR gate (complements are available).

Answer: 1

questions.text: Consider the language L given by the regular expression (a+b )* b (a+b )  over the alphabet {a, b}. The smallest number of states needed in a deterministic finite-state automation (DFA) accepting L is ___________.
questions.solution:
The language is "the second-last symbol is b". The DFA must remember the last two symbols: aa, ab, ba, bb [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] 4 states (all distinguishable).

Answer: 4

questions.text:
Consider a database that has the relation schema EMP (EmpId, EmpName, and DeptName). An instance of the schema EMP and a SQL query on it are given below.
The output of executing the SQL query is _____.
questions.solution:
The inner query counts employees per department: AA 4, AB 3, AC 3, AD 2, AE 1. Every (DeptName, Num) pair is in that result, so all five rows are kept.

AVG = (4 + 3 + 3 + 2 + 1) / 5 = 13 / 5 = 2.6

Answer: 2.6

questions.text:
Consider the following CPU processes with arrival times (in milliseconds) and length of CPU burst (in milliseconds) as given below:

If the pre-emptive shortest remaining time first scheduling algorithm is used to schedule the processes., then the average waiting time across all processes is ________ milliseconds.
questions.solution:
SRTF: P1 0-3 (4 left); P2 (3) preempts, runs 3-6; at 6: P1 4, P3 5, P4 2 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] P4 6-8; P1 8-12; P3 12-17.

Waiting: P1 = 12 [latex]-[/latex] 0 [latex]-[/latex] 7 = 5, P2 = 0, P3 = 17 [latex]-[/latex] 5 [latex]-[/latex] 5 = 7, P4 = 0 [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] average = 12 / 4 = 3

Answer: 3

questions.text:
Consider a two-level cache hierarchy with L1 and L2 caches. An application incurs 1.4
memory accesses per instruction on average. For this application, the miss rate of L1 cache 0.1, the L2 cache experiences, on average, 7 misses per 1000 instructions. The miss rate of L2 expressed correct to two decimal places is ___________.
questions.solution:
Per 1000 instructions: memory accesses = 1400, L1 misses = 0.1 [latex]\times[/latex] 1400 = 140. These 140 go to L2, which misses 7 times.

L2 miss rate = 7 / 140 = 0.05

Answer: 0.05
